problem: For the function $f(x,y)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+x\sqrt{y},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(\frac{1}{4},4).$

activity_context.topic_title: Computing Partial Derivatives Using the Rules of Differentiation

feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the constant multiple rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}{e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}{e}^{y})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}{e}^{y}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x(\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})\cdot {e}^{y}+{y}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y})) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x((2y)\cdot {e}^{y}+{y}^{2}\cdot {e}^{y}) \\  & =(2y+{y}^{2}){e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(0,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y}{|}_{(0,2)} & =(2\cdot 2+{2}^{2}){e}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\  & =8{e}^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =8{e}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
